answer: Neighborhood Cutoff Ranking. Each agent's reputation score is weighted by the number of distinct clusters its counterparties span; an identity whose neighbors sit inside one small island of the graph gets its influence capped regardless of volume. Reaching the visibility zenith requires sustained links across separate regions, and a fresh identity lands in a hollow region with no cross-cluster edges. An attacker must therefore run many identities over time to build genuine spanning connectivity, paying continuous coordination and delay per identity rather than a one-time fee.
